message.content: As context length increases, decode throughput typically decreases due to the quadratic scaling of attention computation and the growing memory bandwidth required to process longer sequences. Longer prompts increase the computational load per token during generation, as the model must attend to a larger number of previous tokens, leading to higher latency and reduced tokens-per-second. Additionally, memory access patterns become less efficient with longer contexts, further impacting throughput. Optimizing attention mechanisms, such as using sparse attention or flash attention, can mitigate these effects, but the fundamental trade-off between context length and decode speed remains significant.
